claims.claim: Codeine, the closest morphinan analog with an absolute oral bioavailability record, had F = 80.5% in healthy subjects after oral and intravenous administration, supporting F ≥ 20% for the query hydromorphone, which shares the morphinan scaffold, 4,5-epoxy bridge, N-methyl group, and phenolic C3 substitution.

L2 codeine records show relative oral-vs-intramuscular bioavailability of about 50-55% in smokers and nonsmokers; these are not absolute F values but demonstrate substantial oral absorption and do not contradict F ≥ 20%.

Other opioid analgesics in the evidence set all exceeded the 20% threshold: pentazocine ~0.68-0.70 in cirrhosis (C09, C16, C25, C54), meperidine 0.80-0.87 in cirrhosis (C11, C21, C24, C41, C51, C56, C59), and meptazinol 27.9% in cirrhosis (C10, C36, C55).

No supplied record provides affirmative evidence of F < 20% for hydromorphone or a close analog; the low-bioavailability L2 record for norethisterone in rats and rabbits (C29) concerns a different steroid and is not transferable to this morphinan query.

evidence_gaps: No direct hydromorphone absolute oral bioavailability record is present; the prediction relies on structural transfer from codeine and class-level opioid data.
Codeine differs from hydromorphone at C3 (methoxy vs phenol) and C6 (hydroxy vs ketone), which may alter first-pass metabolism; no matched oral-vs-IV hydromorphone exposure data are supplied.
Several supporting opioid values were measured in cirrhosis patients and may not reflect healthy-subject F, though all remain above 20%.
L2 codeine values are relative to intramuscular administration, not absolute F, so they are context rather than direct endpoint evidence.
